completion_reason: Three material architecture and integration decisions remain unresolved.

questions.label: Provider eligibility
questions.context: Queue groups span direct, LAN mesh, and PeerJS providers.
questions.question: When is a provider eligible to receive a lease?

choices.text: Require healthy heartbeat, capability match, capacity, and trusted endpoint policy.
Require heartbeat and capability match only.
Allow any configured provider; fail and retry at runtime.

questions.label: Memory promotion
questions.context: Execution memory is isolated; only validated records may enter versioned workflow memory.
questions.question: What authorizes promotion into workflow memory?

choices.text: Validation passes plus explicit approval, recorded as an immutable Run event.
Validation passes automatically; approval is optional.
Workflow stage policy alone decides automatic or approval-gated promotion.

questions.label: Lease ownership
questions.context: FIFO atomic leases must remain consistent across heterogeneous provider transports.
questions.question: Where should queue ordering and lease state be authoritative?

choices.text: NexusCentral alone owns durable ordering, leases, expiry, and retries.
Each Router group owns its own durable lease ledger.
Providers coordinate leases; NexusCentral only records outcomes.
